_evidence: FINAL mapping for the Asia Economic Review legacy import (aer-launch W4). No site id, no image host: those live in the owner-held overlay ~/aer-private/overlay.json. Decided 20-10-26 from the discovery result (01-discover-aer.sql, 644 rows: 276 published, 311 archived never published, 53 draft, 4 rejected) and two owner answers. (1) status: published only (owner); everything else is SKIP, later catch-up runs pick up what the old site publishes before cutover. (2) categories: the old site only has briefings, corporate-asia and essays; their subsection slugs equal the new taxonomy, so briefings and corporate-asia pass through unchanged (pillar = old section, sub-section = old subsection) and essays goes to asia-watch with the same sub-section. The other entries cover sections with zero rows today, in case a catch-up run meets them. (3) authors: even split over the 4 staff names (owner); legacy bylines (Lena Ho 247 of 276 published) are not kept. (4) tags: only the 6 approved tags (D6). (5) bodyImages and archivedAs are moot (0 body images; archived rows are skipped). (6) old origin is the apex host (the old sitemap uses it). Old pages with no articles (/team, /the-long-view, /the-review-interview, /data-annual, /partner-insights) get hand-written redirects at cutover, not from this file. (7) body.reflowMaxChars 380 (owner review 20-10-26): the old DB holds each section as one block (0 of 1,268 sections contain a newline) and the old site split it into paragraphs at render time; grouping sentences while a paragraph stays <= 380 chars reproduces the old breaks exactly in 150 of 161 sampled sections.
